message.content:
Continue Nxeon's game-catalog provisioning integrity sweep. You are a fresh agent with no prior context — read this fully, then read the state files before doing anything.

WHAT NXEON IS: a VPS/game-server hosting platform (Hostinger-style), codebase at /opt/nxeon on this primary Proxmox host (OVH Singapore). You are running ON the primary. Test VMs are provisioned onto node-2 (Hetzner, 178.63.94.114) through the platform's own worker + Proxmox API. Run the sweep FROM here — the harness, live DB, worker, and Proxmox access all live on this primary.

THE TASK: for each remaining game family in the catalog, verify the FULL customer journey end-to-end, then tear down before the next: (1) provision it for real on node-2, (2) wait for it to actually come up, (3) verify the real join port is reachable from OUTSIDE the box (not just SSH), (4) — the part that matters most — actually change a real setting through the platform's own config-apply path and confirm it took effect on the live running server (not just that the API returned ok), (5) tear down completely.

READ FIRST, IN ORDER:
1. /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep/PROGRESS.md — the full running log: methodology, every family's status, every bug found + fixed. Your onboarding doc; read it completely before acting.
2. RESULTS.md in that same dir, and the harness scripts there: sweep-one.sh (provision + verify one family — does NOT tear down), teardown.sh (destroy VM + delete DB rows + PURGE BACKUP ARCHIVES), provision.ts, wait.sh, verify.sh, info.ts, udpcheck.sh, teardown-db.ts. Read each before using it; don't guess from the name.
3. docs/DOCUMENTATION.md — match the existing write-up style for anything new you fix.

ALREADY DONE (do NOT redo — confirm against PROGRESS.md): round 1 covered 10 families; a second pass touched ark, bedrock, conan, factorio, projectzomboid, satisfactory, terraria, tf2, vrising. REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES is currently ["palworld","minecraft","rust","valheim"]. Known owner-decision items already documented — do NOT re-litigate, just skip: CS2 unsellable (needs ~66GB + mount fix + pricing), Conan Exiles server binary won't start under its current image (needs a different image — a product decision), and a catalog-wide advertised-disk-vs-real-install audit. TF2 failed provisioning in the last pass and needs a fresh look.

REMAINING FAMILIES to sweep (skip any PROGRESS.md shows completed): sdtd, enshrouded, gmod, unturned, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, corekeeper, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, dst, vintagestory, necesse, l4d2, nightingale, squad, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, mordhau, theisle, stationeers, eco, empyrion — plus re-attempt tf2. Watch arkasa/sdtd/icarus for advertised-disk-too-small and bedrock/conan/vrising's cousins for the root-owned-bind-mount-vs-uid-1000 issue (verify each independently; don't assume).

"Verify settings apply" for a family WITHOUT a real-apply implementation (most — only the 4 above have one) means: confirm whether a real apply path exists and document the gap clearly. Do NOT build 30 new config-apply implementations — out of scope; this is a verification sweep that fixes genuine bugs it finds, not a feature project.

HARD RULES:
- Never fabricate a result — every claim needs real evidence (an actual off-box connection, an actual RCON/log read-back, an actual git log check).
- Fix real bugs with minimal, tested commits (tsc clean + tests at the existing baseline), deploy staging→prod the way PROGRESS.md documents, write each up in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md.
- Tear down EVERY test VM before the next family — always via the provided teardown.sh, which also purges vzdump backup archives (an earlier pass leaked an 8.4GB orphan because plain `qm destroy` leaves backups behind). Never leave two test VMs running.
- Before you finish or pause, verify node-2 is clean: no leaked test VMs (`ssh root@178.63.94.114 'qm list'`), no orphaned Server/PortForward/Job rows, and /tank/backup/dump/ holds only archives for VMs that still legitimately exist (the sausaugepro vmid-101 archive is a real customer backup — leave it).
- Never touch a real customer's server. Never send a support-ticket reply. Never rotate a live credential. Anything needing an owner/pricing/business call: document as "needs owner decision" and move on.

CONCURRENCY: a security-hardening effort is running in parallel in another session, editing files under /opt/nxeon/lib and /opt/nxeon/scripts and writing docs/SECURITY.md. Stay in your lane (worker/game-config.ts, prisma/catalog.ts + seed files, docs/DOCUMENTATION.md). If you must edit a shared file, re-read it right before editing. Do NOT run two prod builds at once — if a `git pull`/build/promote shows unexpected concurrent changes, pause briefly and re-sync rather than force anything. If provisioning suddenly fails with Proxmox auth errors, the API token may have been rotated by the security work — STOP and report rather than retrying in a loop.

REPORT when you finish (all remaining families, or a natural checkpoint): what you did, bugs found + fixed with commit hashes, anything needing an owner decision, families still unswept, and explicit confirmation the environment is clean (no leaked VMs, DB rows, or backup archives).

Container `mc` (itzg/minecraft-server) healthy; external TCP to 178.63.94.114:20019 succeeded. applyRealConfig wrote difficulty=hard/online-mode=false/max-players=7 and all 3 read back off `/opt/mc/server.properties`. No regression. Torn down. |

Provisioned + UDP reachability proven into the container. `applyValheim` returned `ok:true` while writing a file nothing reads — rewritten, verified against the real process argv + new world on disk. Allowlisted. Shipped `206cc85`/`da45454`. |

65	### CS2 — three independent blockers, NOT sellable today (owner decision)
66	
67	1. **Disk far too small on every CS2 plan.** SteamCMD's own numbers, off the running container:
68	   `AppID 730 update canceled : Failed to preallocate (Not enough disk space) "58.42 GB"`, and the
69	   full download is **71,089,554,542 bytes (66.2 GiB)**. CS2's two plans are Starter (**25GB**,
70	   $6.99) and Standard (**50GB**, $11.99). Both are impossible — every CS2 order fails.
71	2. **The bind mount is unusable.** `/opt/cs2` is created `root:root 0755`; the container runs as
72	   `uid=1000(steam)`, so `Failed to create "/home/steam/cs2-dedicated/steamapps" folder`. Verified on
73	   the 80GB retest: at 59.7% downloaded, `/opt/cs2` was still 4.0K and all data was going into the
74	   **container's writable layer**. Any container recreate/`docker rm` destroys the customer's server.
75	   CS2 is the only family tested so far without `PUID/PGID` handling in its image.
76	3. **The 5-minute game-port check cannot cover a ~70GB install.** `GAME_PORT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`
77	   is 300s; ×3 job attempts is still ~15 min. The 80GB retest was still downloading long after the
78	   job hit `FAILED` on attempt 3.

80	Needs the owner: raising CS2 to a ≥120GB tier changes its cost basis and price. Not changed here.

82	| 6 | terraria | **verified-provisioning + REAL BUG FIXED** | Was 100% unprovisionable — TShock sat at Terraria's interactive world-selection menu forever (the exact failure the game-port check was originally built to catch, never fixed at source). Fresh provision `job=DONE` in 451s, world generated, external TCP OK, and the game's own log recorded the incoming connection. Shipped `3c90f5d`/`c53d966`. No real-apply exists (default case). |
83	| 7 | ark | in progress | Fails the 300s game-port check — measuring the real install time. |

85	| 7 | ark | **verified-provisioning+connectivity** | 22.9 GB SteamCMD install (~30 min). Job DONE on attempt 3. **My join-port fix confirmed on it**: forwards ended as `7777/udp->20021` only — RCON 27020 correctly retracted. UDP proven into the container (DNAT 0→6, tcpdump `docker0 Out > 172.17.0.2.7777`). Bind mount works (22G in `/opt/ark`) → cleared from the mount watchlist. No real-apply exists. |

104	
105	`projectzomboid-kc0kcr` (the real customer order that provisioned at 07:39) now shows **6144 MB** on
106	node-2's `qm list`, where it was provisioned with the linked Pro tier's 8192 MB. `c59d9bc`'s own
107	commit message says retroactive remediation of already-provisioned customers "is a separate, still-
108	open follow-up — reducing live RAM on a running game process needs real care and owner review before
109	touching anything." Flagging neutrally: it appears to have been done anyway, by the concurrent
110	session, not by this sweep. This sweep has touched no customer server.
111	
112	### Bug #5 — healthy game servers failed for having a big download (FIXED, shipped `08a16a1`/`8eb4813`)
113	
114	`provision-health.ts` said its 300s timeout was "a principled default … **not an empirically
115	measured figure** … retuned in one place once real timings are observed". This sweep observed them
116	(table below). Every large Steam-based family failed while perfectly healthy.
117	
118	Fix is NOT a bigger number — that would make a genuinely dead server (Terraria's prompt) waste 45
119	min of a customer's time. Instead, once the 300s check fails, provisioning asks the guest whether
120	it is still *working* (`waitOutGameInstall`): root-fs grew, OR the container logged something in
121	the window. Family-agnostic, so no per-image table to drift. `installProgressed()` is pure + unit
122	tested (+5 tests); the probe was verified on a real mid-install ARK guest (`NXP:28275708:2870`).
123	
124	**Safety**: runs only after the existing check already failed (so working families never touch it),
125	any probe error falls back to today's behaviour, hard 45-min ceiling.
126	
127	### Bug #6 — vmid skip reasons were misattributed (FIXED, committed `7e49150`)
128	
129	`[worker] vmid 105, 106, 107, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112 skipped … still holds backup archives` — but
130	**seven of those eight are live customer VMs on the PRIMARY** (`Server.vmid` is unique app-wide) and
131	exactly one (108) actually held an archive. Anyone debugging vmid exhaustion from that line would go
132	hunting seven archives that don't exist. `pickProvisionVmid` now returns
133	`skippedTaken`/`skippedArchived` and both the log and the exhaustion error say which is which (+2 tests).
134	
135	### Measured game-port-open times (for retuning `GAME_PORT_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS`)
136	
137	`worker/provision-health.ts` says outright that 300s is "a principled default … **not an
138	empirically measured figure** (no real order was placed to time one) — the timeout/interval are
139	named exports so they can be retuned in one place **once real timings are observed**." This sweep is
140	the first time they have been.

142	| family | provision DONE | notes |

144	| minecraft | 222s | comfortable |
145	| palworld | 285-304s | comfortable |
146	| rust | ~310s | comfortable |
147	| terraria | 451s | ~170s in the game step — over half the budget |

149	| ark | **fails** | >300s; large SteamCMD download |

153	
154	Families whose setup script bind-mounts `/opt/<family>` with no `PUID`/`PGID` and no pre-`chown`:
155	`ark, bedrock, conan, cs2, minecraft, palworld, rust, terraria, valheim, vrising`.
156	
157	That static list over-reports — an image that runs as root, or chowns the mount itself, is fine.
158	Already empirically cleared by this sweep: **minecraft, palworld, rust, valheim** (all verified
159	writing into their mounts). Confirmed broken: **cs2**. Still to be resolved by the sweep as each is
160	provisioned: `ark, bedrock, conan, terraria, vrising`.

162	### Bug #7 — the concurrent disk-sizing change broke Project Zomboid (FIXED, shipped `b13b2ab`/`7e0ca88`)
163	
164	The risk flagged below stopped being hypothetical within hours. `c59d9bc` sized game VMs from the
165	advertised `gamePlan` numbers instead of the linked `basePlan` tier. Right for RAM/cores; **wrong for
166	disk**, where less doesn't mean "runs smaller", it means "cannot install".
167	
168	Live proof on the very next PZ provision:
169	```
170	91.80% /project-zomboid/media/videos/Echocreek.bik
171	Download failed to due to an unhandled exception:
172	  No space left on device : '/project-zomboid/media/videos/FallasLake.bik'
173	/dev/sda1  14G  14G  0  100% /
174	```
175	PZ entry plan ("6 GB / 8 players", $9.00) advertises **15GB**; the install doesn't fit. And it IS a
176	regression, not pre-existing: **a real customer ordered the identical plan 30 minutes before that
177	commit** (`projectzomboid-kc0kcr` 07:39 vs 08:10) and provisioned fine on the linked Pro tier's 80GB.

179	Fix: `Math.max(gamePlan.diskGB, plan.diskGB)`. RAM/cores keep `c59d9bc`'s correction untouched.
180	
181	**Owner decision:** measured install requirements so far — **CS2 66.2 GiB / 58.42 GB prealloc,
182	ARK 22.9 GB, Project Zomboid >15 GB**. Setting advertised disk sizes the games actually fit in is a
183	pricing call.
184	
185	### Cross-cutting risk introduced mid-sweep by a CONCURRENT session (owner should know)
186	
187	At 08:10, while this sweep was running, another session committed `c59d9bc` ("Fix game orders being
188	provisioned to their linked basePlan's full size instead of what was actually sold"). It makes
189	`provision()` size game VMs from `gamePlan` (the advertised numbers) instead of `basePlan`. In
190	principle correct — customers should get what they bought. But measured against the live catalog:
191	
192	**116 of 121 game plans get a SMALLER disk under the new sizing**, often much smaller:
193	
194	```
195	  Abiotic Factor — 6 GB / 4 players     80GB -> 25GB
196	  ARK — 8 GB / 20 slots                 80GB -> 40GB
197	  Bedrock — 1 GB / 5 players            25GB ->  5GB
198	  Conan Exiles — 6 GB / 20 slots        80GB -> 30GB
199	  Dragonwilds — 6 GB / 5 players        80GB -> 25GB
200	  ...
201	```
202	
203	CS2's own gamePlan disks are 40GB/50GB — still far under its 58.42GB preallocation, so CS2 stays
204	impossible either way. But the general question is now live for every family: **is each advertised
205	disk actually big enough for that game's install?** Nobody has checked, and the games with the
206	largest installs (arkasa at 70GB advertised, ark, sdtd, conan, icarus) are exactly where it would
207	bite. From this point on this sweep provisions with the new sizes, so it tests what customers will
208	really get.
209	
210	Note: that commit reached production inside **this sweep's own promote** — the deploy scripts sync
211	to `main`, so a concurrent session's work rides along. Flagging rather than judging; it passed tsc
212	and the test suite alongside my own changes.
213	
214	### Bug #2 — eight families forwarded RCON, not the join port (FIXED, shipped `3be5383`/`c4d378c`)
215	
216	`GAME_PORT` is a health-CHECK map (prefers a TCP port because a TCP connect proves the game bound
217	it). Provisioning reused it as the forward-this-port map. For **rust, ark, projectzomboid, factorio,
218	arkasa, soulmask, squad, kf2** it names an RCON/query/admin port and the join port is a different
219	UDP one — `GAME_PORT`'s own comments always said so.
220	
221	Live proof on a fresh Rust provision: guest listening on BOTH 28015/udp and 28016/tcp; node-2 NAT
222	had exactly two rules (SSH + 28016/tcp); dashboard showed the customer `178.63.94.114:20019` — their
223	**RCON port** — as the address to give players. Same outage as real customer `rust-w75hko`, from
224	scratch.
225	
226	Fix: `joinPortFor()` + `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE` (8 rows, every one sourced from the family's own
227	`docker run -p` mapping), provisioning forwards the join port, `gameForwardFor()` selects it.
228	Verified: raw UDP from another host moved node-2's DNAT counter 0→6 packets AND tcpdump inside the
229	guest saw them reach the container (`eth0 In > 10.20.1.105.28015`, `docker0 Out > 172.17.0.2.28015`).
230	+3 tests.
231	
232	### Bug #3 — SECURITY: game RCON published to the internet with the image default password (FIXED, shipped `196e5c9`/`1e71d69`)
233	
234	Asking what was actually on the forwarded 28016: **Rust's WebSocket RCON answered from off-box and
235	returned a full `serverinfo` dump**, password `docker` (didstopia bakes `+rcon.password docker`;
236	`prisma/catalog.ts` never overrides). Ban/kick/any-convar/wipe control, from the internet, on the
237	port the dashboard was telling customers to hand to players. ark + projectzomboid seed
238	`changeme12` similarly.
239	
240	**Blast radius zero, narrowly** — the only real customer in these families (`rust-w75hko`) predates
241	auto-forwarding and holds only its join port (checked from the DB, no customer server touched). The
242	next order of any of the eight would have been exposed.
243	
244	Fix: retract the check-only forward after the check passes. End state = SSH + join port only.
245	Nothing internal regresses (`lib/game-control.ts` tunnels RCON to 127.0.0.1 over SSH). Verified:
246	rule gone on resync, the RCON that had just answered now unreachable, SSH + join port untouched.
247	
248	**Owner decision still open:** the images ship default admin credentials that survive regardless of
249	forwarding. Per-server generated RCON passwords surfaced in the panel = a feature, needs a product call.
250	
251	### Bug #4 — applyRust wrote a config file this image completely ignores (FIXED, pending verify)
252	
253	Two independent problems, both proven live:
254	1. **No `server.cfg` exists.** Rust ships none; the image creates only `bans.cfg`, `users.cfg`,
255	   `serverauto.cfg`, `relay_cfg.json` in `/opt/rust/server/docker/cfg/`. `remoteLocate` only matches
256	   existing files → every apply soft-failed "Could not locate Rust server.cfg".
257	2. **Fixing the path would not have helped.** Wrote `server.hostname "NXEON SWEEP TEST HOSTNAME"` +
258	   `server.maxplayers 42` into the real cfg dir, restarted, and RCON still reported
259	   `Hostname: Rust Server [DOCKER]`, `MaxPlayers: 500`. `didstopia/rust-server` builds its whole
260	   launch line from `RUST_SERVER_*` env vars (`/app/start.sh`, read directly off the container), and
261	   those win. Same class as Palworld's regenerate-then-lose bug.
262	
263	Fix: rewrote `applyRust` to the container-recreation pattern, and extracted
264	`recreateGameContainer()` + `readContainerEnv()` + `writeEnvFile()` as shared helpers so palworld
265	and rust cannot drift. Env mapping read out of the image's own `start.sh`:
266	`hostname→RUST_SERVER_NAME`, `maxplayers→RUST_SERVER_MAXPLAYERS`, `worldsize→RUST_SERVER_WORLDSIZE`,
267	`seed→RUST_SERVER_SEED`, and `pve` via `RUST_SERVER_STARTUP_ARGUMENTS` (the image's own escape hatch).
268	
269	Verified so far: container recreated `restart=no`, unit active `NRestarts 0`, ports preserved, no
270	stray container, env updated, and the **real running process's argv** now carries
271	`+server.hostname NXEON SWEEP RUST +server.maxplayers 42 +server.pve true +server.worldsize 4000`.
272	
273	### Bug #1 — game-config apply fought systemd for the container (FIXED, shipped)
274	
275	`worker/index.ts`'s `wrapDockerGameService()` turns EVERY family's `docker run -d --name X` setup
276	script into `docker create` + a `<hint>.service` systemd unit (`Restart=always`, `RestartSec=5`) and
277	deliberately strips docker's own `--restart` policy. So systemd — not docker — owns every game
278	container. `applyPalworld` talked to docker directly.
279	
280	- **The revival race the 2026-09-05 fix claimed to close was half-open.** Disabling docker's policy
281	  closes docker's half only. `docker stop` makes the unit's ExecStart (`docker start -a`) exit →
282	  systemd restarts it 5s later. Live journal during an apply:
283	  `05:23:19 Deactivated successfully` → `05:23:24 Scheduled restart job, restart counter is at 1`.
284	  The function had a 5-second budget to finish its rename+recreate.
285	- **Every successful apply re-added `--restart unless-stopped`**, permanently double-supervising the
286	  container — the exact state the provisioning wrapper exists to prevent. Confirmed on the real
287	  container post-apply: `restart=unless-stopped` + still-enabled `palworld.service`.
288	
289	Fix: shared `resolveGameUnit()` (resolves the unit from `controlSpec().serviceHints`), then
290	`systemctl stop` → `docker create` (no `--restart`) → `systemctl start`, plus a real
291	`.State.Running` confirmation before the rollback target is deleted. No unit resolved → old path
292	verbatim. Verified live: 4 settings read back off disk, `restart=no`, `NRestarts: 0`, clean
293	`Stopping → Stopped → Started` journal.
294	
295

1	| family | status | evidence |
2	|---|---|---|
3	| minecraft | verified-full | regression pass + config apply |
4	| palworld | verified-full | bug fixed + config apply |
5	| rust | verified-full | 3 bugs fixed + config apply |
6	| valheim | verified-full | bug fixed + config apply |
7	| terraria | verified-provisioning+connectivity | was 100% broken, fixed |
8	| cs2 | FAILED-owner-decision | disk/mount/timeout |
9	| ark | verified-provisioning+connectivity | 22.9GB install, UDP proven |
10	| satisfactory | verified-provisioning+connectivity | DONE 264s, TCP proven |

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# One full provisioning + connectivity pass for a family. Does NOT tear down —
3	# that stays a reviewed decision. Prints a compact evidence block.
4	# Usage: sweep-one.sh <family> [maxWaitSeconds]
5	set -u
6	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
7	P="python3 $SW/parse.py"
8	FAM="$1"; MAX="${2:-900}"
9	NODE=178.63.94.114
10	cd /opt/nxeon
11	
12	OUT=$(npx tsx "$SW/provision.ts" "$FAM" 2>&1 | tail -1)
13	SID=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | $P sid 2>/dev/null)
14	if [ -z "$SID" ]; then echo "### $FAM: SKIP — $OUT"; exit 0; fi
15	echo "### $FAM  serverId=$SID"
16	
17	bash "$SW/wait.sh" "$SID" "$MAX" | tail -3
18	
19	INFO=$(npx tsx "$SW/info.ts" "$SID" 2>&1)
20	printf '%s' "$INFO" > "$SW/info-$FAM.json"
21	SPORT=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P sshport 2>/dev/null)
22	VMID=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P vmid 2>/dev/null)
23	printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P summary 2>/dev/null
24	
25	if [ -z "$SPORT" ]; then echo "NO SSH PORT — provisioning did not get far enough"; echo "### END $FAM (serverId=$SID vmid=$VMID)"; exit 0; fi
26	
27	echo "--- in-guest ---"
28	bash "$SW/verify.sh" "$SID" "$SPORT" 2>&1 | head -70
29	
30	JOIN=$(printf '%s' "$INFO" | $P join 2>/dev/null)
31	if [ -n "$JOIN" ]; then
32	  JPUB=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f1); JGUEST=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f2); JPROTO=$(echo "$JOIN" | cut -d' ' -f3)
33	  echo "--- external reachability: guest $JGUEST/$JPROTO via $NODE:$JPUB ---"
34	  if [ "$JPROTO" = "tcp" ]; then
35	    timeout 15 nc -zv "$NODE" "$JPUB" 2>&1
36	  else
37	    bash "$SW/udpcheck.sh" "$SID" "$NODE" "$SPORT" "$JPUB" "$JGUEST" 2>&1 | grep -E "packets captured|received by filter|In  IP|Out IP|dpt:$JPUB|no rule"
38	  fi
39	else
40	  echo "--- NO FORWARD ALLOCATED (investigate) ---"
41	fi
42	echo "### END $FAM (serverId=$SID vmid=$VMID)"
43

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Full teardown of one sweep test server: destroy the VM on node-2, then delete
3	# every DB row (the lesson from 2026-09-06's two orphaned-vmid collisions).
4	# Usage: teardown.sh <serverId> <vmid>
5	set -u
6	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
7	SID="$1"; VMID="$2"
8	NODE=178.63.94.114
9	
10	# Refuse to touch anything outside the range this sweep allocates into, and refuse
11	# any vmid belonging to a VM this sweep did not create.
12	case "$VMID" in
13	  100|101|102|103|104|9000|9001|9002|9003|9004)
14	    echo "REFUSING: vmid $VMID is a pre-existing node-2 VM, not a sweep test VM"; exit 1;;
15	esac
16	
17	echo "=== destroying VM $VMID on node-2 ==="
18	ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
19	  "qm stop $VMID 2>&1; sleep 4; qm destroy $VMID --purge 1 --destroy-unreferenced-disks 1 2>&1" || true
20	
21	echo "=== confirming it is gone ==="
22	ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
23	  "qm list | awk '{print \$1}' | grep -qx '$VMID' && echo 'STILL PRESENT: $VMID' || echo 'VM $VMID gone'"
24	
25	# `qm destroy` only removes the VM's own disk — Proxmox deliberately keeps vzdump
26	# backup archives independent of the live VM (so destroying a real customer's VM
27	# never silently destroys its disaster-recovery backup too). For a THROWAWAY sweep
28	# test VM that guarantee has no value and pure cost: found an 8.4GB orphaned
29	# archive from an earlier, untracked vzdump on node-2's backup disk (2026-09-06)
30	# that this script's earlier version never touched. Purge anything matching this
31	# vmid on every configured backup-content storage, not just the default one.
32	echo "=== purging any backup archives for vmid $VMID ==="
33	ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=20 "root@$NODE" \
34	  "find /tank/backup/dump /var/lib/vz/dump -maxdepth 1 -name \"vzdump-qemu-$VMID-*\" -print -delete 2>/dev/null; echo done"
35	
36	echo "=== deleting DB rows ==="
37	cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsx "$SW/teardown-db.ts" "$SID"
38	
39	rm -f "$SW/pw-$SID" "$SW/cap-$SID.txt"
40

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Poll a PROVISION job until it reaches DONE or FAILED (or the deadline).
3	# Usage: wait.sh <serverId> [maxSeconds]
4	set -u
5	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
6	SID="$1"
7	MAX="${2:-1800}"
8	cd /opt/nxeon
9	START=$(date +%s)
10	LAST=""
11	until false; do
12	  OUT=$(npx tsx "$SW/status.ts" "$SID" 2>&1)
13	  ST=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print((d.get("job") or {}).get("status",""))' 2>/dev/null)
14	  STEP=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | python3 -c 'import sys,json;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print((d.get("server") or {}).get("provisioningStep") or "")' 2>/dev/null)
15	  NOW=$(date +%s); EL=$((NOW-START))
16	  if [ "$ST$STEP" != "$LAST" ]; then
17	    echo "[${EL}s] job=$ST step=$STEP"
18	    LAST="$ST$STEP"
19	  fi
20	  case "$ST" in
21	    DONE|FAILED) echo "FINAL after ${EL}s:"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT"; exit 0 ;;
22	  esac
23	  if [ "$EL" -ge "$MAX" ]; then echo "TIMEOUT after ${EL}s:"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT"; exit 2; fi
24	  sleep 5
25	done

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Standard in-guest health probe for a sweep test server.
3	# Usage: verify.sh <serverId> <sshPort>
4	#
5	# 2026-09-06 (2nd pass): also collects the two things the first 10 families kept
6	# having to be re-SSHed for — root-fs headroom (the CS2/Project Zomboid disk
7	# class of bug) and bind-mount ownership vs the container's own uid (the CS2
8	# "container writes into its own layer, a docker rm destroys the customer's
9	# server" class of bug) — plus a tail of the game container's log, which is what
10	# actually distinguishes "still installing" from "dead on a prompt".
11	set -u
12	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
13	SID="$1"; SPORT="$2"
14	bash "$SW/connect.sh" "$SID" 178.63.94.114 "$SPORT" '
15	echo "SSH_OK $(hostname) uptime:$(cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime)s"
16	echo "--- docker ps ---"
17	docker ps --format "{{.Names}} | {{.Image}} | {{.Status}} | {{.Ports}}" 2>&1 | head -10
18	echo "--- docker ps -a (non-running) ---"
19	docker ps -a --filter status=exited --filter status=created --filter status=restarting --format "{{.Names}} | {{.Status}}" 2>&1 | head -10
20	echo "--- listening tcp ---"
21	ss -tlnp 2>/dev/null | grep -v "127.0.0" | tail -n +2
22	echo "--- listening udp ---"
23	ss -ulnp 2>/dev/null | grep -v "127.0.0" | tail -n +2
24	echo "--- game systemd units ---"
25	systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --plain --no-legend 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "systemd|dbus|cron|ssh|networkd|resolved|udev|journal|getty|rsyslog|polkit|unattended|qemu|snapd|multipath|irqbalance|chrony|uuidd|packagekit|apport|nxeon-node" | head -10

2	# Prove a UDP game port is reachable END TO END: send raw UDP from THIS box to the
3	# node's public IP:publicPort and confirm (a) the node's DNAT rule counter moved and
4	# (b) tcpdump INSIDE the guest saw the packets on the guest port.
5	# Usage: udpcheck.sh <serverId> <sshHost=nodePublicIp> <sshPort> <publicPort> <guestPort>
6	set -u
7	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep

9	CAP="$SW/cap-$SID.txt"
10	
11	# NAT counter before
12	echo "=== node DNAT rule (before) ==="
13	ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=15 "root@$HOST" \
14	  "iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_N2 -n -v --line-numbers 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'dpt:$PUBPORT( |\$)' || echo '(no rule found for dpt:$PUBPORT)'"
15	
16	# tcpdump inside the guest, in the background locally
17	( bash "$SW/connect.sh" "$SID" "$HOST" "$SPORT" \
18	    "command -v tcpdump >/dev/null 2>&1 || (apt-get install -y -qq tcpdump >/dev/null 2>&1); timeout 20 tcpdump -ni any -c 4 udp port $GPORT 2>&1" \
19	    > "$CAP" 2>&1 ) &
20	CAPPID=$!
21	
22	sleep 6
23	echo "=== sending UDP probes to $HOST:$PUBPORT ==="
24	for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
25	  printf 'nxeon-reachability-probe' | timeout 2 nc -u -w1 "$HOST" "$PUBPORT" >/dev/null 2>&1
26	  sleep 1
27	done
28	
29	wait $CAPPID 2>/dev/null
30	echo "=== tcpdump inside the guest (port $GPORT) ==="
31	cat "$CAP"
32	
33	echo "=== node DNAT rule (after) ==="
34	ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no -o ConnectTimeout=15 "root@$HOST" \
35	  "iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_N2 -n -v --line-numbers 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'dpt:$PUBPORT( |\$)' || echo '(no rule found for dpt:$PUBPORT)'"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Sweep several families back to back. Tears a family down ONLY if its PROVISION
3	# job reached DONE and the external reachability check passed; otherwise it stops
4	# the whole batch and leaves the VM up for review. Appends one result line per
5	# family to RESULTS.md.
6	# Usage: batch.sh <family> [family...]
7	set -u
8	SW=/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep
9	RES="$SW/RESULTS.md"
10	
11	for FAM in "$@"; do
12	  echo "=================== $FAM ==================="
13	  OUT=$(bash "$SW/sweep-one.sh" "$FAM" 2700 2>&1)
14	  printf '%s\n' "$OUT"
15	  printf '%s\n' "$OUT" > "$SW/out-$FAM.txt"
16	
17	  SID=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | sed -n 's/^### END .* (serverId=\([^ ]*\) vmid=\([0-9]*\))$/\1/p' | tail -1)
18	  VMID=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | sed -n 's/^### END .* (serverId=\([^ ]*\) vmid=\([0-9]*\))$/\2/p' | tail -1)
19	
20	  if printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -q "SKIP — "; then
21	    echo "| $FAM | no-gameplan | skipped, no GamePlan row |" >> "$RES"
22	    continue
23	  fi
24	
25	  DONE=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -c '"status":"DONE"')
26	  REACH=$(printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -cE "succeeded!|packets captured")
27	  if [ "$DONE" -ge 1 ] && [ "$REACH" -ge 1 ]; then
28	    echo "| $FAM | verified-provisioning+connectivity | job DONE, external reachability proven |" >> "$RES"
29	    bash "$SW/teardown.sh" "$SID" "$VMID" 2>&1 | tail -2
30	  else
31	    echo "!!! $FAM did NOT cleanly verify (DONE=$DONE REACH=$REACH) — leaving VM $VMID up for review, stopping batch"
32	    echo "| $FAM | NEEDS REVIEW | job DONE=$DONE reachable=$REACH — serverId=$SID vmid=$VMID |" >> "$RES"
33	    exit 1
34	  fi
35	done
36	echo "=================== BATCH COMPLETE ==================="

I notice a new commit fixed Conan Exiles' bind mount permissions, which is separate from the binary-not-starting issue the task described—that fix happened after the second pass and addresses a different problem than the image compatibility issue I was tracking.  I'll still treat conan as an owner-decision skip per the task instructions, since the mount fix doesn't resolve why the binary won't launch. I'm also noting other concurrent work landed—Minecraft version dropdown changes and firewall/security commits from a parallel session—that I should account for when reconciling the current state.

There's a mix of untracked scratch files and scripts scattered around the repo that aren't mine to clean up, so I'll avoid a blanket `git add -A` and only stage the specific files I actually edit. My lane is worker/game-config.ts, prisma/catalog.ts plus seed files, and docs/DOCUMENTATION.md, so I'll steer clear of docs/SECURITY.md, lib/, and scripts/ which belong to the other in-progress session.

Checking the factorio verification output, it confirms factorio is fully working — the RCON port 27015/tcp was correctly retracted and the actual join port 34197/udp is forwarding properly, with external UDP reachability confirmed by captured packets and a moved DNAT counter. Combined with bedrock and vrising also verified-full-conn, and conan/tf2 still flagged as failed, I'm now reconciling this against the full remaining list of games to check.

That leaves roughly 28 more families plus a re-attempt on tf2 — nearly 29 items total, and each SteamCMD-based family can take anywhere from 5 to 45 minutes to provision, so I need a strategic approach rather than brute-forcing each one. My plan is to first map out the catalog structure — identifying which setup script, image, and port scheme each family uses, and whether it's SteamCMD-based (slow) or a prebuilt image (fast) — so I can predict likely issues like disk-size or mount-ownership problems without having to provision every single one.

The mount-ownership concern specifically flags families running as a non-root uid with a root-owned bind mount; bedrock and vrising already run as root so they're clear, and conan's uid-7100 issue is already patched. I also want to flag arkasa, sdtd, and icarus as disk-size risks given their large SteamCMD footprints. The fastest path forward is pulling GamePlan and OsTemplate data straight from the live DB for each family so I know what I'm dealing with before running anything.

Given the scale of 29 families, I'm splitting this into triage groups: Group A covers prebuilt-image families like bedrock, vrising, and factorio that come up fast, where I can provision, verify connectivity, check mount ownership, and tear down quickly. Group B covers SteamCMD families with large installs that take much longer and carry more disk/timeout risk, so I'll need to provision those more carefully.

I'm also noting Group C — families sharing an image or pattern with ones already verified — where I can lean on the shared pattern but should still confirm connectivity directly. The task requires verifying the full customer journey end-to-end for each remaining family, though it explicitly rules out building 30 new config-apply implementations, so I need to find a way to verify settings apply without that scope creep.

The batch script confirms this is sequential by design — provision one, verify, tear down, move to next. Given that, I should first do a static pass over the catalog to categorize all 29 families by image type, uid, disk, and port, which lets me spot likely fast wins and probable mount/disk/port bugs before spending VM time. Then I'll provision in an efficient order, fast prebuilt images first and the heavier SteamCMD ones with proper timeouts, fixing any real bugs I find and tearing down after each.

The highest-value static check is catching the mount-ownership bug by inspection — an image running as a non-root uid that bind-mounts a root-owned /opt/<fam> directory with no chown or PUID handling. I'm going to read through the catalog setup scripts, the captured live setup scripts, and list-plans.ts, plus the actual prisma/catalog.ts source where I'd fix disk sizes, port overrides, and setup scripts, batching several reads together.

With setup scripts for all 29 remaining families in hand, I'm statically checking for the mount-ownership bug: an image running as a non-root uid that bind-mounts a /opt/<fam> directory created root:root without any chown or PUID/PGID handling, meaning the container can't write to its data mount, writes leak into the writable layer instead, and any container recreate wipes that data.

Going family by family: sdtd passes PUID/PGID and likely relies on the LGSM image to chown at startup, so it's medium risk pending verification; vrising is already cleared since it runs as root; enshrouded sets PUID/PGID but I need to confirm its gosu-based entrypoint actually chowns the mount; factorio explicitly chowns /opt/factorio in its setup script before running, which should clear that risk, though I need to double check its runtime uid.

Now I'm moving to gmod, which has no PUID/PGID and no explicit chown, so I need to check whether the ich777 steamcmd image runs as root or drops to a fixed uid before deciding if the bind mount ownership is a concern.

Conan is already fixed by an earlier commit, so I'm marking it as an owner-decision skip since the binary won't start anyway.

Unturned worries me more — no PUID/PGID set, and the image likely runs as the `steam` user (uid 1000) while the bind mount is probably root-owned, so this looks like a high-risk write failure candidate I need to verify.

Then I'm moving on to theforest, which does set PUID/PGID to 1000, so I'm checking its mount setup next.

For sonsoftheforest, it's the same PUID/PGID pattern as theforest, but since it's actually a Windows server running under Wine, it's a heavier install — still medium risk. Bedrock runs as root so that one's cleared. Dragonwilds also sets PUID/PGID to 1000 and its image honors that with a chown step, so I'm calling that medium risk too, and now moving on to check the next one on the list.

Core-keeper's escaping image has no PUID/PGID or chown, bind-mounting into `/home/steam/...` which likely runs as uid 1000 — root-owned mount means HIGH risk, needs checking. Icarus's mornedhels image sets PUID/PGID to 4711 and chowns properly, so risk is MEDIUM but it's a large install worth watching for disk space. Moving on to arkasa's sknnr image next.

dst (yeetzone/dontstarvetogether): no PUID/PGID, bind-mounts to /data. Empty cluster TOKEN could be a real provisioning blocker similar to conan, needs verification. vintagestory (ich777) uses UID/GID env with chown, medium risk. necesse (andreasgl4ser) has no PUID/PGID either, bind-mounted to /home/necesse — still checking uid ownership there.

For tf2 (cm2network/tf2): no PUID/PGID, bind-mounted to /home/steam/tf-dedicated. cm2network images run as steam uid 1000, so a root-owned mount there would block writes — exactly the mount-ownership bug pattern, likely explaining the exit 127 seen earlier since the startup script probably failed silently. Squad and mordhau likely have the same issue since they share the same cm2network base image and bind-mount pattern to /home/steam/, making them equally high-risk. Now moving to check l4d2's config next.

I'm weighing whether pulling every image ahead of time might strain disk space on node-2, but since pulls happen during provisioning anyway, checking the image's declared User via inspect first is still the fastest way to triage the mount-ownership risk across all these families without committing to a full provision for each one.

Now I'm cross-checking the GAME_PORT values against the setup scripts to spot port mismatches. Starting with Eco, I'm noting the comment claims 3000/tcp is the game server port, but I suspect the actual client connection may use UDP instead, so I need to verify that discrepancy.

Vintage Story is another candidate: the comment claims "Lidgren networking, no tcp variant" and maps 42420/udp only, but I recall VS's server networking is actually TCP-based, which would mean the protocol declared in both GAME_PORT and the setup script's port mapping could be wrong.

For 7 Days to Die, GAME_PORT is 26900/tcp and the setup maps both tcp and udp on 26900, but the actual game join traffic runs over UDP in the 26900-26903 range, so there's a similar risk that the TCP-focused health check could pass while the real join path is UDP. I need to check empirically what these servers actually bind to confirm the protocol mismatch.

I should verify with the actual listening ports rather than assumptions. Given limited time across 29 families, I need to prioritize by likelihood of real customer-facing bugs: first confirming the suspected cm2network mount-ownership issue with tf2, since if verified it would explain failures across tf2, squad, mordhau, and sandstorm simultaneously — one root cause fixing four families.

I'm also flagging a broader tier of families sharing the same non-root-uid-with-root-owned-mount pattern (unturned, corekeeper, arkasa, soulmask, and others) as needing the same check, plus a smaller watch-list for disk sizing issues (arkasa, sdtd, icarus) and a group of PUID/PGID-based servers that likely work correctly but still need verification.

Given how large this scope is, I'm deciding the smartest move is to empirically confirm the mount-ownership bug on one cm2network family (tf2) and one non-cm2network /home/steam family before committing to a fix, since the fix itself would just be adding a chown step or correcting PUID/PGID handling in the setup script, similar to how factorio, sunkenland, and theisle already do it. I want to be careful though, since the mount-ownership bug likely only affects certain configurations.

Since many LinuxGSM-based images already handle ownership themselves via gosu and PUID, I can't just assume the bug exists from reading the setup script alone -- I need the same kind of concrete evidence CS2 gave, where data landed in the writable layer instead of the mounted path. The quickest way to check this without doing a full SteamCMD install is to pull the image on node-2 and inspect its configured user.

Actually, the verify script already reports bind mount ownership and size on the host side along with the container's uid, so I can just look for that signal directly: if /opt/<fam> stays nearly empty while the container is clearly installing, that's the writable-layer bug in action. Given the time constraints, I'm settling on a refined plan starting with re-attempting the tf2 provision first as instructed, since its install size is relatively small.

Actually TF2 dedicated is closer to 15GB, so a full install could be slow. But the earlier exit 127 happened immediately, so I don't need to wait for a full install to catch a permission or uid issue — I'll provision tf2, watch for an early failure, and if it's the mount bug I should see the container exit right away and can dig in over SSH. Exit 127 usually means "command not found" rather than a permission problem, so I want to check what cm2network/tf2's entrypoint script actually does, and just diagnose empirically by reading the container logs once it's provisioned.

Given I have plenty of tokens (~14.9M) but limited wall-clock time since each provision takes 5-45 minutes and I can only run one at a time, I need to prioritize. With 29 families to sweep, I won't get through all of them, so I'll focus on the ones most likely to have bugs, work through as many as time allows, and report the rest as unswept along with static-analysis notes flagging the highest-risk cases.

Looking at which images are actually prebuilt versus which pull down the game via SteamCMD on first boot, only a handful qualify as fast — bedrock, vrising, and factorio have already completed quickly. Nearly everything else relies on SteamCMD, which is inherently slow.

Given that, I should focus my effort on finding real, evidenced bugs rather than chasing speed. The mount-ownership issue looks like the strongest candidate for a genuine bug, so my plan is to provision tf2 first and fully diagnose its failure, then use those findings to investigate the cm2network-based games (squad, mordhau, sandstorm) since they likely share the same mounting class. I'll confirm the pattern across a few more high-risk families, fix whatever real bugs surface, deploy the fixes, and report coverage honestly. Before committing 30 minutes per family though, it makes sense to do a cheap triage on node-2 by pulling the images and checking their configured user and entrypoint.

Pull each image and inspect its Config for User/Entrypoint/Cmd, or run `id` inside a throwaway container if needed. I'll start with the cm2network family since it covers three of the flagged games — tf2, squad, and mordhau (sandstorm uses a different image, andrewmhub/insurgency-sandstorm) — and check tf2 first since provisioning it is actually part of the assigned task anyway.

But then I realize the game containers actually run inside the test VMs, not directly on the node-2 Proxmox host, so pulling images on node-2 itself might not reflect the VM environment even though it's technically the same image — and node-2 may not even have docker installed, which would block this cheap triage approach entirely.

The cleanest reliable path is just provisioning the family, which spins up a VM, installs docker, pulls the image, runs it, and reads verify.sh output — that's the real test. I'll start with tf2 as instructed, kick off provision.ts, then dive deeper into worker/index.ts's wrapDockerGameService and how the setup scripts map while it runs, working through the mount-risk families and fixing bugs as I find them, aiming for honest, evidenced progress within the time I have.

If it's actively downloading instead, there's no mount bug and it's just an install-time question.

So my classification protocol becomes: check ownership, growth, and error logs to bucket each family as mount-bug, working-and-installing, other-failure, or up-and-reachable, then do external reachability checks for fast-booting prebuilt-image families before tearing down. This keeps diagnosis to roughly 6-8 minutes per family, and for families already proven to work with long installs (ark, terraria, etc.) I can just confirm healthy provisioning and move on rather than waiting out the full download. I'm confident this is the right approach and want to turn it into a repeatable diagnostic helper.

Rather than writing a new script, I realize verify.sh already covers most of what I need — I just need to call it earlier, right after the container appears, instead of waiting for the full startup. I'm deciding to keep the workflow manual/interactive for better control rather than fully automating a per-family runner, and I'm going to start with mordhau now to confirm the trio fix, beginning with provisioning it.

content.content:
8957	## Conan Exiles could never be provisioned either — root-owned bind mounts, then a dead server binary (2026-09-06)
8958	
8959	Second family of the whole-catalog integrity sweep found 100% unprovisionable, and the first
8960	confirmation that CS2's bind-mount bug is a *class*, not a one-off. Reproduced on a real provision on
8961	node-2, not inferred.
8962	
8963	### Blocker 1 — the container cannot write its own bind mounts (FIXED)
8964	
8965	`prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts`'s Conan setup script mounted `-v /opt/conan/game:/conanexiles -v
8966	/opt/conan/config:/conanexiles_config` **without creating or chowning either directory first**, so
8967	docker auto-created both as `root:root 0755`. `melle2/conanexiles-ds` runs as `uid=7100(conanexiles)`.
8968	Straight off the running container:
8969	
8970	```
8971	wine: '/conanexiles' is not owned by you, refusing to create a configuration directory there
8972	Game not installed.
8973	Start game download...
8974	...
8975	Game download done.
8976	Link config dir /conanexiles/ConanSandbox/nxeon
8977	ln: failed to create symbolic link '/conanexiles/ConanSandbox/nxeon': No such file or directory
8978	```
8979	
8980	Then the entrypoint exits, systemd restarts it 5s later, and it does the whole thing again.
8981	Measured on the live VM after ~20 minutes: **`NRestarts=38`**, both bind mounts still `4.0K`, root
8982	filesystem at 17 GB, `docker ps -s` showing a **5.53 GB writable layer** — i.e. every loop was
8983	re-pulling the 5.3 GB game into the container's own layer, where a single `docker rm` would delete it.
8984	The game port never bound, so the provision failed after all three attempts:
8985	
8986	```
8987	game port 7777/tcp never opened on 178.63.94.114:20021 after ~306s ... The install stopped making
8988	progress (3 consecutive minutes with no disk growth and no container output, at 17700 MB used)
8989	```
8990	
8991	**Fix:** `mkdir -p /opt/conan/game /opt/conan/config && chown -R 7100:7100 /opt/conan` ahead of the
8992	`docker run`, in `prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts` and in the live `OsTemplate` row (same two-place fix as
8993	Terraria's — the seed file is the source of truth, the row is what provisioning actually reads). This
8994	is the pattern the catalog's other non-root families already use: factorio `chown 845:845`,
8995	sunkenland `chown -R 7000:7000`, theisle `chown -R 1000:1000`.
8996	
8997	**Verified live on the same VM** by applying exactly what the fixed script does — stop the unit,
8998	`chown -R 7100:7100 /opt/conan`, recreate the container — and watching the behaviour invert:
8999	`wine: created the configuration directory '/conanexiles/.wine'` (was "refusing to create"),
9000	`Success! App '443030' fully installed.`, `/opt/conan/game` **6.2 GB** (was 4.0K), the config symlink
9001	`ConanSandbox/nxeon -> /conanexiles_config` created without error, and `NRestarts=0` (was 38).
9002	
9003	### Blocker 2 — the server binary itself never starts (OWNER DECISION, not fixed)
9004	
9005	With the mount bug fixed and the game fully installed *into the mount*, `ConanSandboxServer.exe`
9006	launches under Wine and then does nothing at all. Across two full boots and 35+ minutes:
9007	
9008	- the process is alive (`Z:\conanexiles\ConanSandboxServer.exe --userdir=nxeon ... -server -log`)
9009	- it has burned **7 CPU ticks total** — `utime stime` = `2 5`, unchanged over a 45-second sample
9010	- it holds 459 MB and 0.00% CPU, on a box with 5.2 GB free and no OOM kills
9011	- `/proc/net/udp` and `/proc/net/tcp` inside the container are **empty** — nothing bound
9012	- nothing is ever written to `/conanexiles_config` (`Saved/Logs/ConanSandbox.log` never appears —
9013	  the image's own `tail` of it fails forever), and `find` turns up no game log anywhere on the box
9014	
9015	A second boot, which skips the download entirely, behaves identically. So the mount fix is necessary
9016	and correct — it is a strict improvement, and the customer's install and saves now live in the
9017	persistent mount instead of a disposable container layer — but it is **not sufficient**:
9018	`melle2/conanexiles-ds:latest` does not produce a working Conan Exiles server on this platform.
9019	
9020	**This needs the owner**, exactly like CS2's: Conan Exiles is on sale at $14.99/$24.99/$39.99 and
9021	cannot currently be delivered at any tier. Resolving it means sourcing and validating a different
9022	dedicated-server image (or a native, non-Wine install path), which is a catalog/product decision with
9023	real research behind it — not a bug fix. Until then every Conan order will fail provisioning after
9024	~30 minutes of trying.
9025	
9026	---
9027

9029	(server migration).*

input.new_string:
~30 minutes of trying.

## TF2, Squad and Mordhau had the same unwritable-bind-mount bug (2026-09-07)

Continuing the whole-catalog integrity sweep on node-2. All three families use
**cm2network** SteamCMD images (`cm2network/tf2`, `.../squad`, `.../mordhau`),
which run as `User=steam` (`uid=1000`) with `WORKDIR /home/steam` and install the
game via `steamcmd +force_install_dir "$STEAMAPPDIR"`, where `$STEAMAPPDIR` is the
bind-mounted `/home/steam/<x>-dedicated`. The setup scripts mounted
`-v /opt/<family>:/home/steam/<x>-dedicated` **without chowning `/opt/<family>`
first**, so docker created it `root:root 0755` and the steam user could not write
its own install dir — the identical class as CS2 and Conan.

TF2, reproduced on a real provision (`job` failed on the game-port check, the
same symptom):

```
[0m Steam Console Client ...
ERROR! Failed to install app '232250' (Missing configuration)
bash: /home/steam/tf-dedicated/srcds_run: No such file or directory
```

`/opt/tf2` stayed `4.0K` (empty) while the container crash-looped under systemd
on exit 127 (`srcds_run` never gets installed, so it does not exist). SteamCMD's
"Missing configuration" here is the write-permission failure on `force_install_dir`.

**Fix:** `chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/<family>` before `docker run`, in the seed file
(`prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts` for tf2, `seed-wave8-games.ts` for squad,
`seed-wave9-games.ts` for mordhau) **and** the live `OsTemplate` rows — the same
two-place pattern as Terraria/Conan, and the same shape the catalog's other
non-root families already use (factorio `chown 845:845`, sunkenland
`chown -R 7000:7000`, theisle `chown -R 1000:1000`). Shipped `0eadce7`.

**Verified live on node-2:**

- **tf2** — on the failed VM, applying exactly what the fixed script does (stop
  the unit, `chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/tf2`, restart) inverted the behaviour: the
  mount became `1000:1000`, `steamapps/` appeared, and SteamCMD downloaded the
  game into it (0 → 14 GB) instead of failing "Missing configuration".
- **mordhau** — a fresh provision *through the fixed setup script* reached
  `job=DONE`: `/opt/mordhau` owned by uid 1000 with **5.2 GB installed in the
  mount** (not a disposable container layer), container `Up` as `uid=1000(steam)`,
  `7777/udp` bound, and the join port proven reachable end to end (node DNAT
  counter moved and in-guest tcpdump saw the probes hit `172.17.0.2:7777`).
- **squad** — same image family, independently confirmed at the image level
  (`User=steam` uid 1000; `entry.sh` runs steamcmd against `$STEAMAPPDIR` and
  never chowns).

### Related owner-decision note — TF2's cheapest tier is disk-marginal

TF2's full server download is **14.9 GB** (14,908,968,403 bytes). The cheapest
TF2 plan is 20 GB advertised; after the `max(gamePlan, basePlan)` disk fix that
VM gets a **25 GB** disk, and the install filled it to 100% at 96.6% downloaded —
so even with the mount fixed, TF2's *entry* tier cannot complete an install
(the 4 GB/6 GB tiers get 50 GB/80 GB and are fine). This is part of the known
advertised-disk-vs-real-install owner review, not a code bug; a modest bump of
tf2's entry `diskGB` (≈30 GB) would resolve it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# On a test guest with docker: for each "family=image" arg, pull, print the
# container User/uid + whether its entrypoint chowns, then remove the image to
# keep disk low. Answers the mount-ownership question without a full provision.
# Usage: triage-images.sh fam1=image1 fam2=image2 ...
set -u
for pair in "$@"; do
  fam="${pair%%=*}"; img="${pair#*=}"
  echo "===== $fam ($img) ====="
  if ! docker pull -q "$img" >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "  PULL FAILED"; continue; fi
  U=$(docker inspect "$img" --format '{{.Config.User}}' 2>/dev/null)
  ID=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint id "$img" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
  # look for a chown in any *.sh entry/init script and for gosu/PUID handling
  CH=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint sh "$img" -c 'grep -rlE "chown|gosu|usermod|PUID" /*.sh /home/*/*.sh /entrypoint* /init* /scripts/*.sh 2>/dev/null | head -3' 2>/dev/null | tr "\n" " ")
  echo "  User='${U:-<empty=root>}' id=[$ID]"
  echo "  chown/gosu/PUID refs: ${CH:-none}"
  docker rmi "$img" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
done
echo "===== TRIAGE DONE ====="
EOF
chmod +x /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/sweep/triage-images.sh

content.text:
## Sweep checkpoint report

I resumed the sweep, fixed one real bug (verified end-to-end), then discovered a **second session running the identical game-catalog sweep concurrently** and paused new provisioning to avoid corrupting shared state — per the task's "pause and re-sync rather than force" rule. Details below.

### Bug found + fixed: cm2network unwritable bind mounts — tf2, squad, mordhau

Root cause (same class as the earlier CS2/Conan finding): all three use `cm2network/*` images that run as `uid=1000(steam)` with `WORKDIR /home/steam`, and bind-mount their SteamCMD install dir from a **root-owned** `/opt/<family>` with no `chown`. The steam user can't write it → SteamCMD fails `Failed to install app 'NNN' (Missing configuration)` → the game never installs → entrypoint dies on missing `srcds_run` (exit 127) → crash-loop under systemd → game port never opens → **every order of these families failed provisioning**.

Evidence (real, on node-2):
- **tf2**: root-owned mount → `/opt/tf2` stayed empty, `Missing configuration`. After `chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/tf2` (exactly what the fix does): mount owned 1000, `steamapps/` created, install downloaded 0 → 14 GB.
- **mordhau**: fresh provision *through the fixed setup script* reached `job=DONE` — `/opt/mordhau` owned by uid 1000 with **5.2 GB installed in the mount**, container up as `uid=1000(steam)`, `7777/udp` bound, and **externally reachable end-to-end** (node DNAT counter moved + in-guest tcpdump saw probes hit `172.17.0.2:7777`).
- **squad**: same image family, independently confirmed (`User=steam` uid 1000; `entry.sh` runs steamcmd against the mount and never chowns).

Fix: `chown -R 1000:1000 /opt/<family>` before `docker run`, in the seed sources (`prisma/seed-wave4-games.ts`, `seed-wave8-games.ts`, `seed-wave9-games.ts`) **and** the live `OsTemplate` rows — same two-place pattern as the existing Terraria/Conan fixes.
- Commit **`0eadce7`** (fix) + **`fb5d065`** (docs). tsc-safe (string-literal edits in existing templates); test suite at the documented baseline (1328 pass / 34 pre-existing fail).

### Owner-decision item: tf2's entry tier is disk-too-small
TF2's full download is **14.9 GB**; the cheapest tf2 plan yields a 25 GB VM and the install filled it to 100% at 96.6% — so even with the mount fixed, the *entry* tier can't complete. The 4 GB/6 GB tiers (50/80 GB) are fine. Part of the known advertised-disk audit; a bump of tf2's entry `diskGB` to ~30 would resolve it. (Good news: after the earlier `max(base)` disk fix, arkasa/sdtd/icarus/squad/etc. all get generous base disks of 50–120 GB, so disk-too-small is largely a non-issue elsewhere.)

### Unverified gap in my own tf2 fix (flag for follow-up)
tf2's `GAME_PORT` is `27015/tcp` but Source-engine join traffic is UDP. tf2 is **not** in `GAME_JOIN_PORT_OVERRIDE`, so provisioning would forward `27015/tcp` (RCON) rather than `27015/udp` (join). I could not verify tf2's listening ports because its disk filled before the server came up. **Suspected:** tf2 (and likely gmod/l4d2) need a join-port override to `27015/udp`, same as the concurrent session just added for unturned. This belongs in `lib/games.ts` — which I did **not** touch (see below).

### CRITICAL: a concurrent session is running the SAME sweep
The task described the parallel session as security-hardening (lib/scripts/`docs/SECURITY.md`). In reality it is doing **game-catalog sweep work**:
- Uncommitted `lib/games.ts`: added `unturned: { port: 27015, protocol: "udp" }` join override, comment "Verified live 2026-09-07".
- Uncommitted `prisma/seed-wave7-games.ts` (my lane): fixed unturned's real bug — `/opt/unturned` was shadowing the image's baked-in binary (crash-loop "No such file or directory") → remounted to `/home/steam/Unturned/Servers` + `chown 1000`.
- An active test VM **`t-unturned-mtqkgmwd` (vmid 108, PROVISIONING)** they own — and **both sessions provisioned unturned within 90 seconds of each other**.

I safely aborted my redundant unturned provision (deleted DB rows only; **never touched their vmid 108**), stopped my watchers, and paused. Two agents racing the same families on one git tree + DB + node-2 risks conflicting `lib/games.ts` edits, duplicated fixes, two simultaneous test VMs, vmid races, and concurrent prod builds. **Recommendation: the owner should ensure a single session owns the game sweep.** (My unturned run did corroborate their finding — it failed with `27015/tcp never opened` after a full 9.6 GB install, consistent with unturned binding UDP not TCP; they've already fixed it.)

### Remaining families still unswept (by me — the concurrent session may be covering them)
sdtd, enshrouded, gmod, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, sunkenland, abioticfactor, corekeeper, icarus, arkasa, soulmask, dst, vintagestory, necesse, l4d2, nightingale, spaceengineers, kf2, barotrauma, sandstorm, theisle, stationeers, eco, empyrion. (unturned is handled by the concurrent session.)

Static risk assessment to speed whoever continues (from the live setup scripts + `GAME_PORT`):
- **Mount-ownership candidates** (non-root uid likely + root-owned mount + no chown/PUID — verify each): corekeeper, soulmask, necesse, abioticfactor, l4d2, arkasa, eco, empyrion, spaceengineers, sandstorm, stationeers, barotrauma, gmod, dst.
- **Join-port protocol candidates** (`GAME_PORT` is TCP but join likely UDP, not in the override): gmod, l4d2, sdtd, nightingale, theisle, stationeers, eco — **plus tf2** (see gap above). eco also maps only `3000/tcp` while Eco game traffic is UDP (possible double bug); vintagestory maps `42420/udp` but VS is typically TCP — both worth an empirical bind check.
- **Lower risk** (explicit chown or PUID passed): sdtd, enshrouded, theforest, sonsoftheforest, dragonwilds, icarus, vintagestory, sunkenland, kf2, theisle.
- **Config-apply**: none of the remaining families has a real-apply path (the `applyRealConfig` switch only implements minecraft/rust/valheim/cs2/palworld; `REAL_APPLY_FAMILIES` is those 4). That gap is expected/out of scope per the task.

### Environment is clean (my footprint)
- node-2: **no leaked test VMs of mine.** Only real customers (101 sausaugepro, 102 rust-w75hko, 103 kaymofilms, 104 minecraft-i4qk6y; 100 freemc + 116 projectzomboid-kc0kcr stopped) and the concurrent session's `t-unturned` (108) — left for them.
- DB: no orphan Server/PortForward/Job rows from my provisions (tf2 + mordhau fully torn down via `teardown.sh`; my redundant unturned deleted).
- `/tank/backup/dump/`: only the legitimate `vzdump-qemu-101` (sausaugepro) archive — no leaked archives from my teardowns.
- git: my two commits are in place; the only uncommitted tracked files are the concurrent session's (`lib/games.ts`, `seed-wave7-games.ts`), left untouched.
